Players to watch out for:



Among players to watch, Rajat Patidar has been in sensational form this season. With 142 runs in just three innings at an average of 71 and a striking rate of 200, he has been the driving force behind RCB’s batting. His ability to accelerate while maintaining consistency makes him a dangerous player, particularly in the middle overs where he can shift the momentum rapidly.

For MI, Ryan Rickelton has shown promising signs at the top. Scoring 98 runs in three innings at a strike rate of 168, he has provided aggressive starts that set the tone for the innings. While his average of 32 suggests room for improvement in converting starts, his intent and ability to take on bowlers early make him a key player in MI’s batting lineup.
 

Key Matchups:



The battle between Virat Kohli and Jasprit Bumrah has been one of the most intriguing contests in the IPL in recent years. Since 2020, Bumrah has managed to keep Kohli relatively quiet, conceding just 38 runs across 7 innings while dismissing him three times. This reflects Bumrah’s ability to outthink even the best in the game, especially with his variations and pinpoint accuracy. For RCB, Kohli’s role as the anchor is crucial, but MI will once again bank on Bumrah to break that backbone early.

Another key matchup is Bhuvneshwar Kumar versus Hardik Pandya, which brings a classic battle of control versus power. Bhuvneshwar has done a commendable job of restricting Hardik, conceding just 35 runs in 8 innings and dismissing him twice. His ability to swing the ball and execute slower deliveries makes him a tricky opponent, especially against a batter like Hardik who thrives on pace. This duel could be decisive in the death overs, where momentum often swings games.


Head to Head:



Looking at the recent head-to-head record, Mumbai Indians and Royal Challengers Bengaluru have been evenly matched since 2022. Out of the five encounters, RCB have edged ahead with three wins compared to MI’s two. This reflects how closely fought this rivalry has become, with no clear dominance and games often being decided by small moments or individual brilliance.

Game Preview:

Mumbai Indians come into this contest searching for rhythm. After a convincing opening win, Hardik Pandya’s side has stumbled with back-to-back defeats, exposing concerns in both departments. While their batting boasts experience through Rohit Sharma and Suryakumar Yadav, consistency in the middle overs remains a question. More worrying has been their bowling, overly reliant on Jasprit Bumrah, who continues to be their biggest weapon across phases. Support from the likes of Trent Boult and Shardul Thakur will be crucial if MI are to regain control.

RCB, on the other hand, appears far more settled despite their recent setback against Rajasthan Royals. Led by Rajat Patidar, the defending champions have showcased depth and firepower. Their top order featuring Virat Kohli and Phil Salt has been instrumental, while their explosive middle order, powered by Tim David, gives them the ability to recover or accelerate at will. The return of Josh Hazlewood strengthens their bowling, particularly in death overs.

The Wankhede surface is expected to favor batters early on, with dew likely to play a role in the second innings, making chasing slightly advantageous. However, recent trends suggest teams batting first with big totals can still dictate terms. With both sides looking to bounce back from defeats, expect a high-intensity contest where momentum swings quickly. MI will rely on home advantage and experience, while RCB’s balanced unit and finishing power might just give them the edge in this blockbuster encounter.

Rajat Patidar (RCB Captain):
“It feels incredible to be here at the Wankhede Stadium - the atmosphere, the fans, playing in a completely packed house is something special. It’s a different feeling altogether.
There was great clarity in our approach. The way Virat bhai and Salt got us off to such a strong start put us firmly in control. I chipped in with a quick cameo as well, and overall it was a complete team effort.
People often say I enjoy playing spin, but honestly, I really back myself against fast bowlers. This is a beautiful surface to face pace, and I thoroughly enjoy batting on tracks like this.”



Hardik Pandya (MI Captain):
“Yes, we lost too many wickets, and at the same time, we conceded far too many runs, which meant we were always playing catch-up. Over the last couple of games, both with bat and ball, we haven’t been leading the game - we’ve been reacting. That’s something we need to reflect on and fix to find the momentum we’re missing.
We’ve got a couple of days off now, and a lot needs to be rethought because clearly a few things aren’t working. Even though we’ve won the toss in some games, we need to explore other options as a batting and bowling group. On these kinds of wickets, good batting and good bowling are the key - irrespective of the toss.
The focus is on improving our power play performance, because right now we’re falling behind early in both disciplines. We’ll look at all options ahead of the next game. Bringing in Rutherford was exciting for us - we know his power and potential, and the way he’s batting gives us confidence and flexibility going forward.”


Royal Challengers Bangalore completely dominated the first innings with a blistering batting display. Phil Salt and Virat Kohli gave them a dream start, adding 120 runs for the opening wicket. Salt was particularly destructive, smashing 78 off just 36 balls, while Kohli contributed a steady 50. The fireworks continued when skipper Rajat Patidar played a sensational knock of 53 at an extraordinary strike rate of 265, further accelerating the scoring. Tim David then added the finishing touches with a quickfire 34 from 16 balls, propelling RCB to a massive total of 240

Chasing such a daunting target, the Mumbai Indians began well with Rickelton and Rohit Sharma putting up 72 for the first wicket. However, they struggled to maintain the required run rate and lost wickets in the middle overs. RCB’s spinners, Krunal Pandya and Suyash Sharma, tightened the grip by sharing three crucial wickets. Despite a late counterattack from Sherfane Rutherford, who hammered an unbeaten 71 off 31 balls, MI fell short, finishing at 222. RCB secured victory by 18 runs, thanks to their explosive batting and disciplined bowling.

The contest within the contest could play a decisive role in this clash. Avesh Khan vs Shubman Gill is a key matchup, with Avesh having dismissed Gill four times in eight IPL innings since 2021, conceding just 65 runs, a battle that often sets the tone early. Another intriguing duel is Prasidh Krishna vs Rishabh Pant, where Prasidh has dismissed Pant twice in three innings while giving away only 18 runs since 2021. These faceoffs promise intensity and could significantly influence the course of the LSG vs GT encounter.

Players to Watch Out For:

For Gujarat Titans, Jos Buttler has been in strong form in TATA IPL 2026. In three innings, he has scored 116 runs at an average of 39 and a strike rate of 156, with a highest score of 52, making him a crucial top-order threat. On the LSG side, Aiden Markram has impressed with his consistency and impact, scoring 78 runs in three innings at an average of 36 and an identical strike rate of 156, with a top score of 45. Both batters have the ability to shift momentum quickly in their team’s favor.

Head to Head:

Since 2022, the rivalry between Lucknow Super Giants and Gujarat Titans has been closely contested. The two sides have faced each other seven times, with GT holding a slender edge after winning four matches, while LSG have claimed three victories. This narrow margin highlights how competitive the fixture has been, often going down to key moments and individual performances.



Game Preview:

Gujarat Titans and Lucknow Super Giants square off in another intriguing Indian Premier League contest, with both teams aiming to strengthen their position in the points table. Since entering the IPL in 2022, this fixture has quickly become competitive, producing both high-scoring games and closely fought encounters. Gujarat Titans hold a slight edge in the overall head-to-head record, although Lucknow have managed to close the gap with strong performances in recent seasons. 
 
Gujarat Titans rely heavily on a stable top order led by captain Shubman Gill, whose ability to anchor the innings has been a key factor in their success. Sai Sudharsan’s consistency at the top provides solidity, while the middle order features several power-hitters capable of accelerating in the final overs. With the ball, Gujarat’s attack is well balanced, featuring pace options who strike early and quality spin that controls the middle overs, a combination that has worked effectively across conditions.
 
Lucknow Super Giants, led by Rishabh Pant, bring an aggressive approach to the matchup. Their batting strength lies in a powerful middle order, with players such as Nicholas Pooran and Mitchell Marsh capable of changing the game within a few overs. Lucknow’s bowling unit is built around pace, supported by spinners who look to exploit pressure situations, especially on slower surfaces.
Matchsummary.PostMatchCommentary:
Prasidh Krishna (Player of the match):
The most important thing is the team’s victory. We’ve been working hard and doing a lot of things right, trying to play a good brand of cricket. I’m just benefiting from the pressure created by the other bowlers. With experience, you learn to react to situations, but a lot also comes from discussions within the team - there’s so much knowledge in the dressing room to draw from.
It all comes down to hard work in practice - bowling a lot in the nets, trusting your skills, and putting in the effort even when the body feels tired. It was definitely a tough afternoon, but a win makes it all worthwhile

Shubman Gill (GT Captain):
Absolutely. The way we bowled in the power play was excellent, and the pressure we maintained through the middle overs was outstanding. When the bowlers perform like that, it makes my job much easier. Rashid, in particular, has been phenomenal - every time the game seems to drift, he pulls us right back in. He builds pressure with dot balls, picks up wickets, and is extremely tough to score off.
In the first six overs, it’s easy to get carried away, but it’s important to stay grounded and focus on doing the simple things well. Rashid did that brilliantly today - his first over was spot on, and in his third, he stuck to his lengths and executed perfectly, which really swung the game our way. Siraj bowled very well too, and while KG went for a few runs, his lengths were still good. Sometimes in T20 cricket, you get unlucky - inside edges or well hit shots can happen.
The closing overs weren’t easy. We probably conceded about 10 extra runs at the back end when they were six or seven wickets down. Still, if you’d offered us 160 at the start of this pitch, we would have taken it without hesitation


Rishab Pant (LSG Captain):
We were probably short of runs, but full credit to them - they bowled really well. On a wicket like this, a total of around 170 to 180 is actually a very good score. Unfortunately, wickets kept falling, and they managed to apply constant pressure by striking regularly. As I said, on this surface, that score was par, and there were still opportunities in the game. I wouldn’t say we were completely out of it, but we failed to grab those moments when they came.”
“Without doubt, it’s a very strong batting unit. The tournament has only just begun, so there’s no need to put pressure on anyone. Especially when it comes to the senior players - they understand their roles and what’s required. There are phases when things don’t click, but the trust and belief within the group is strong. We’re confident it’ll come together soon, and the environment in the camp remains very positive.”



The Super Giants began their innings with energy, thanks to Aiden Markram and Rishabh Pant, but their momentum was repeatedly disrupted by the Titans’ disciplined pace attack. Prasidh Krishna was the standout performer, claiming four wickets while conceding only 28 runs, and he was well supported by Ashok Sharma and Mohammad Siraj, who ensured the Super Giants were restricted to a modest total of 165.

When it was the Titans’ turn to bat, Shubman Gill carried forward his excellent form, converting it into another fluent half-century. He was joined by Jos Buttler, who quickly found his rhythm and matched Gill with a brisk fifty of his own. The Super Giants struggled to contain the aggressive batting display, with only Prince Yadav showing notable resistance through his determined bowling. Ultimately, the Titans chased down the target comfortably, securing victory with eight balls remaining.

Players in the Spotlight:
When it comes to key players, KL Rahul stands out for his consistency against Chennai Super Kings. In 15 innings, he has amassed 630 runs at an average of 45 and a strike rate of 142.9, including six half-centuries, numbers that underline both reliability and impact at the top of the order. For the Men in Yellove, Sarfaraz Khan has been in sensational form in T20 cricket since December 2025, piling up 428 runs in just 10 innings at an average of 53.5 and an explosive strike rate of 202.8, with five scores of 50 or more, which is one 50+ score in every 2 innings.



 

Openers Crucial Against Spin Threat:

The contest could well hinge on how effectively the openers handle the opposition’s spin attack. KL Rahul has shown clear control against Noor Ahmad in the IPL, scoring 42 runs off 28 balls without being dismissed at a strike rate of 150, and could play a key role in neutralizing the Afghan spinner. On the other side, Ruturaj Gaikwad has been particularly dominant against Kuldeep Yadav, striking at over 200 without losing his wicket. Additionally, the CSK skipper has performed well against both Kuldeep Yadav and Axar Patel, scoring 89 runs at a strike rate of 161.8 with just one dismissal. With both sides relying heavily on their spinners, the ability of these openers to dictate terms early could prove pivotal in shaping the flow of the game.

 

Head to Head since 2022:
In recent seasons, the head to head battle between Chennai Super Kings and Delhi Capitals has been closely contested. Since 2022, CSK hold a slight edge with three wins to Delhi’s two, but the momentum has notably shifted in Delhi’s favour. The Capitals have come out on top in the last two encounters, including a landmark victory at MA Chidambaram Stadium last season, which was their first win at the venue in 15 years.

 

 

As the spotlight shifts to the second game of the day in the Indian Premier League, all eyes will be on a fascinating clash between Chennai Super Kings and Delhi Capitals at Chepauk.

Chennai Super Kings find themselves in unfamiliar territory this season. Three games in, they are yet to register a win and currently sit at the bottom of the table, a position rarely associated with the 5 time champions. However, there are signs of promise. CSK have crossed the 200 run mark in each of their last two outings, with their young brigade stepping up and delivering with the bat.

Returning to their fortress at MA Chidambaram Stadium could be just the reset they need. Traditionally dominant at home, CSK will be hoping the familiar conditions help them address their bowling, which has been their biggest concern so far this season. They have conceded runs at the highest economy rate this season and also possess the least effective strike rate with the ball, an area that will need urgent correction if they are to turn their campaign around.

On the other side, Delhi Capitals have had a more encouraging start. They began their campaign with back to back wins before suffering a heartbreaking loss in their previous game, which went down to the very last ball. Despite that setback, Delhi will take plenty of confidence from their bowling unit, which has been instrumental in their success so far. In fact contrary to CSK, DC currently boast the second best economy rate in the tournament and strike once every 18 balls. Their batting, too, is beginning to find rhythm. Sameer Rizvi has been a standout performer, playing a key role in both of their victories, while KL Rahul returned to form in emphatic fashion with a brilliant 92 in the last game.

With momentum on their side, Delhi Capitals will be eyeing another strong performance and will take confidence from their recent success at this venue, having conquered Chepauk not too long ago last season. As CSK look to revive their campaign at home and Delhi aim to continue their impressive run, this contest promises to be a compelling battle between a side searching for answers and another brimming with belief.

Axar Patel (Delhi Capitals Captain):
"We began well but losing quick wickets after the powerplay completely broke our momentum and that made the chase difficult. Wickets falling in clusters meant we were always playing catch up and could not rebuild the innings properly. The batters did a decent job overall but fielding proved to be the difference in the match for us. Credit to the bowlers for restricting them to that score even though they had set batters on a good wicket. A couple of dropped catches hurt us badly and while the pitch stayed similar with slight dew later, they executed their plans better than us."


Chennai Super Kings produced a commanding all round performance at Chepauk, defeating Delhi Capitals by 23 runs in a match that revolved around a monumental innings from Sanju Samson and disciplined control at key moments.

Batting first after being asked to set the total, Chennai posted an imposing 212 for 2 at a run rate of 10.6. Sanju Samson delivered one of the finest knocks of the season, remaining unbeaten on 115 from 56 balls, an innings studded with 15 fours and four sixes at a strike rate above 205. He held the innings together from start to finish, accelerating seamlessly through the middle and death overs. Ayush Mhatre provided strong support before retiring out on 59 from 36 deliveries, while Shivam Dube added late firepower with 20 off 10 as Chennai scored 87 runs in the final eight overs. Delhi struggled for control, conceding 10.25 an over overall, with no bowler going under eight an over.

Delhi’s chase began brightly but lost shape through the middle overs. Pathum Nissanka struck 41 off 24 balls and KL Rahul added 18, helping Delhi reach 61 inside five overs. Tristan Stubbs kept hopes alive with a well paced 60 from 38 balls, but wickets at regular intervals stalled momentum. Jamie Overton turned the game decisively with the ball, returning outstanding figures of 4 for 18 from four overs, while Anshul Kamboj claimed 3 for 35 to apply consistent pressure.

Heinrich Klaasen remains a key figure for Sunrisers Hyderabad. In TATA IPL 2026 so far, he has scored 145 runs at an impressive average of 48 while striking at 148, including two half-centuries that have repeatedly rescued SRH from trouble.

For Punjab Kings, the spotlight shines on Arshdeep Singh. He boasts an excellent record against SRH, having picked up 15 wickets in 11 matches at an average of 22 and an economy of 7.8. His ability to strike early and close out innings could be decisive once again.



Battles that decide the game
One of the most intriguing duels tonight will be between Shreyas Iyer and Harshal Patel. In a short but telling battle, Harshal has dismissed Shreyas three times in just 14 balls, conceding only 17 runs, making this matchup a potential momentum changer in the middle overs. Chahal has had the upper hand, removing Kishan three times in 32 deliveries, even though the batter has scored 55 runs, setting up a fine contest between attack and control.



Head-to-Head since 2021
Since the 2021 season, Sunrisers Hyderabad have enjoyed a clear edge over Punjab Kings. The two sides have met eight times in this period, with SRH winning six of those contests while PBKS have managed just two victories, a trend Punjab will be keen to overturn in New Chandigarh.


Match number 17 of the TATA IPL 2026 sets up a compelling evening at New Chandigarh as the runners-up of the last two seasons come face to face. Sunrisers Hyderabad, finalists in 2024, take on Punjab Kings, who finished second best in 2025, and the contest promises intensity, urgency and plenty of unfinished business.


Punjab Kings walk in with confidence flowing. Two wins from completed matches and a no result that slipped away only because of rain have placed them comfortably in the top half of the table. Their rise has been consistent rather than sudden, and since the 2025 season, only defending champions RCB have boasted a better overall record. The batting unit has been firing from the outset, with Priyansh Arya, Prabhsimran Singh and Shreyas Iyer all among the runs, while Cooper Connolly’s presence at the top has added balance and firepower. Yet one uncomfortable stat looms large. PBKS have lost their last four meetings against SRH, including one last season where dominance still did not translate into victory.


Sunrisers Hyderabad arrive with pressure mounting. Their top order has yet to truly click this season, and the bowling has lacked control in crucial phases. The saving grace has been the calm and power of Heinrich Klaasen and Nitish Kumar Reddy, a partnership that has repeatedly rescued the side when early wickets fell. Their only win so far came against a struggling KKR, but SRH know momentum can shift with one complete performance.

Form meets history under the New Chandigarh lights. Will Punjab finally break the SRH hoodoo and stay unbeaten, or will Sunrisers once again find a way to spoil the party when it matters most?

Punjab Kings pulled off a stunning chase in New Chandigarh, overpowering Sunrisers Hyderabad by six wickets in a run fest that swung wildly but was ultimately settled by fearless intent and sustained momentum.

Sunrisers Hyderabad set the tone with a blistering start after being put in to bat, racing to 105 without loss in the powerplay. Abhishek Sharma produced one of the most explosive innings of the season, smashing 74 off just 28 balls at a strike rate above 260, reaching his fifty in only 18 deliveries. Travis Head supported with 38 from 23 as the opening stand crossed 120 in 8.1 overs. The middle phase was anchored by Heinrich Klaasen’s 39 off 33, while Aniket Verma chipped in with a rapid 18, lifting Hyderabad to a formidable 219 for 6 at nearly eleven an over.

Punjab’s response matched the violence. Priyansh Arya tore into the attack with 57 off 20 balls, while Prabhsimran Singh struck 51 from 25, taking Punjab to 93 without loss in six overs. After a brief slowdown, Shreyas Iyer took command with a superb unbeaten 69 off 33 balls, striking five fours and five sixes. He found support from Shashank Singh’s unbeaten 16 as Punjab crossed the target in 18.5 overs.

Both sides scored at over ten an over for long phases of the game, but Punjab’s deeper acceleration and clarity in the chase made the difference in a high class thriller where the margin was narrow but the intent unmistakable.

MATCH PREVIEW

Match number 14 of the TATA IPL 2026 brings a classic contrast to the fore as Plus Two meets Minus Two, with the Arun Jaitley Stadium set to host a contest driven by momentum on one side and desperation on the other. Unbeaten Delhi Capitals welcome Gujarat Titans, who are still searching for their first win of the season, making this a clash rich in urgency and opportunity.

Delhi Capitals enter the fray riding a wave of confidence. Two wins from two games have underlined their growing balance, and Rizvi’s influence has been nothing short of decisive, once again showcasing the true value of the impact player rule. Their bowling unit has stood tall when it mattered most, restricting both Mumbai Indians and the Lucknow Super Giants to below-par totals. The only lingering concern remains the form of KL Rahul, who has looked a touch out of rhythm so far. However, DC found further batting assurance in their last outing as Nissanka teamed up with Rizvi to dismantle Mumbai’s attack, sealing a comfortable six wicket victory.

Gujarat Titans, meanwhile, walk into Delhi with plenty to address. There were encouraging signs in their previous game as Sai Sudharsan returned to form with a fluent 73 and Jos Buttler began to find rhythm. Yet, once Sudharsan fell, the innings unravelled, culminating in a narrow six-run defeat in a high-scoring thriller against the Rajasthan Royals. The probable return of Shubman Gill could provide stability and lift spirits. With the ball, Prasidh Krishna has been the lone shining light, delivering timely breakthroughs and holding GT’s bowling together.

The Arun Jaitley Stadium promises a tight, tactical battle where execution will outweigh reputation. One side aims to protect its spotless record, the other fights to avoid an early season slide. Will Delhi continue their unbeaten march, or do Gujarat finally get off the mark?

Over the last seven or eight months my body has felt great after a good break and my focus has been on landing the ball consistently in the right areas and being able to spin it both ways. The wicket of Rizvi was very satisfying because as a leg spinner you cherish beating a batter with the wrong one after setting it up. Getting Axar Patel out from around the wicket was something I had planned in practice and I was ready to take the risk as long as I hit the right length. When the game got tense towards the end it was about concentrating on every single delivery and giving full commitment to make scoring as difficult as possible."
 


Shubman Gill (Gujarat Titans Captain):
"All three games we have played so far have gone right down to the final over, so it feels really good to get over the line this time. Even during Miller’s innings I believed we could win and the discussion was about choosing between a yorker or a well disguised slower ball which we felt would be harder to hit. In close games every single run matters and even my overthrows that went for five or six runs made a difference, showing how important each effort is in the field. With the wicket being on the slower side we felt two hundred and ten was about ten to fifteen runs above par and big boundaries were not easy to come by, so good bowling was always going to keep us in the game. As for my own batting after the neck issue, I will rest properly and see how I feel when I wake up tomorrow."


Axar Patel (Delhi Capitals Captain):
"It was a very good game of cricket because both teams competed hard and in such tight matches it is difficult to point at one single moment. We could have been smarter as a batting unit, and losing wickets at crucial times ended up costing us the game. When matches are this close small decisions make a big difference and we will learn from it. KL Rahul played a quality knock and kept the momentum going even as wickets fell at the other end without letting the run rate drop. We are playing good cricket overall and I am confident we will finish the job in our next outing."


Gujarat Titans edged past Delhi Capitals in a high-scoring thriller at the Arun Jaitley Stadium, sealing a narrow one-run victory in a contest where momentum swung relentlessly, and margins stayed razor-thin till the final delivery.


Batting first, Gujarat piled up an imposing 210 for 4, driven by sustained excellence from their top order. Shubman Gill anchored the innings with a superb 70 off 45 balls, striking five boundaries to hold the middle overs together. He found explosive support from Jos Buttler, whose 52 off just 27 deliveries lifted Gujarat to 79 inside eight overs. Washington Sundar then stepped up with authority, scoring 55 from 32 balls at a strike rate above 170, as Gujarat scored at over ten an over in 14 of the 20 overs and added 71 runs in the last five.


Delhi’s chase was equally assertive. KL Rahul produced a marathon knock of 92 from 52 balls, bringing up his fifty in 29 deliveries and keeping the target well within sight deep into the innings. Pathum Nissanka added early intent with 41 off 24, while David Miller’s unbeaten 41 from 20 kept the equation alive till the end. Delhi reached 202 by the final over but fell just short at 209 for 8.

Rashid Khan proved decisive with the ball, returning exceptional figures of 3 for 17 at an economy of 4.25, halting Delhi’s momentum during the middle overs. With both teams scoring at more than ten an over overall, Gujarat’s tighter control in key phases ultimately made the difference in a gripping contest decided by the finest of margins.

Head-to-Head (Last 5 Years):



The rivalry between Punjab Kings (PBKS) and Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) has been fairly competitive over the last five years. PBKS holds a slight edge with four wins, while KKR follows closely with three victories, highlighting how evenly matched these two sides have been in recent seasons.

Game Preview:

The clash between Kolkata Knight Riders and Punjab Kings at Eden Gardens sets up a classic battle of momentum versus uncertainty. KKR come into this game searching for answers. Their struggles date back to the end of the 2025 season, and despite reshaping the squad for IPL 2026, results haven’t followed. Two losses to start the campaign have exposed issues in both departments. The batting hasn’t clicked consistently, with key players yet to find rhythm, while the bowling unit has looked vulnerable, conceding big totals in both games. The absence of injured pacers has only added to their concerns, and the team is still trying to find the right balance.

On the other hand, PBKS look like a side in sync. After reaching the final last season, they have carried that momentum forward with two convincing wins. Their top order has been solid, with contributions coming from multiple players, including new recruit Cooper Connolly, who has settled quickly. More importantly, their bowling attack appears well-rounded and experienced, giving them the edge in crunch situations.

A key storyline in this contest will be Shreyas Iyer facing his former side. Having led KKR to a title not long ago, his return adds an emotional layer to an already intriguing matchup.
For KKR, improvement in the middle overs, both with bat and ball, will be crucial if they are to challenge a confident PBKS unit. Meanwhile, Punjab will look to continue their strong start and tighten their grip early in the tournament.

With form and confidence on their side, PBKS start as favourites, but KKR at home remain a team capable of turning things around.

SEASONED STAR POWER 

Virat Kohli remains the ultimate X factor — a right handed run machine who lives for the big moments and thrives under spotlight pressure. Against CSK, his numbers underline his aura: 1,146 runs in 34 matches, a rock solid strike rate of 128, and a highest score of 90* that screams clutch performance. Virat doesn’t just score runs , he controls tempo, sets the vibe, and drags the game into his orbit. Whether it’s anchoring an innings or flipping the switch with back to back boundaries, his presence alone raises intensity levels. Calm face, killer intent , Kohli is still him, and every time he walks in, the momentum meter tilts his way.

Shivam Dube, on the other hand, is pure late order chaos — a left handed finisher built for impact overs and instant damage. In just 6 matches, he’s hammered 215 runs at a blistering strike rate of 160, with a towering 95 showcasing his six hitting range. Dube doesn’t wait around — if it’s in his arc, it’s gone. Against RCB, he’s been the definition of a momentum hack, turning decent totals into scary ones in a flash. No warm up, no hesitation — just clean swings and big vibes. When Dube sets up at the crease, bowlers know the equation can go sideways real quick.

 

RED Vs YELLOW : PLAYER SHOWDOWNS

Virat Kohli vs Noor Ahmed is a clash soaked in tension, temperament, and tactical intrigue. The master right hander against a fearless left arm chinaman — this duel has produced sparks already. Kohli has scored 63 runs off 44 balls, but Noor has landed crucial blows with 2 dismissals, proving he isn’t overawed by reputation. It’s wrist spin versus willow, guile versus greatness. Kohli looks to impose himself with his trademark intensity and strike rotation, while Noor attacks with drift, dip, and daring, dragging the contest into that uneasy middle overs battlefield where one moment can flip the game on its head. Every delivery feels like a chess move calculated, aggressive, and absolutely unforgiving.

Sanju Samson vs Bhuvneshwar Kumar brings together red hot form and seasoned mastery. Samson, the flamboyant right hand opener and reigning ICC T20 World Cup 2026 Player of the Tournament, has scored 62 runs from 42 balls in this matchup alone. But standing in his way is Bhuvneshwar Kumar — the evergreen swing king, deadly with the new ball and ice cold at the death. With 2 dismissals to his name against Samson, Bhuvi’s ability to nip it early and deceive late turns this into a high stakes thriller. It’s fearless shot making versus relentless accuracy , experience and nerve — a rivalry where one perfect over or one mistimed stroke could define the night.

MATCH PREVIEW

M Chinnaswamy Stadium sets the stage for a heavyweight clash as defending champions Royal Challengers Bengaluru square off against five-time champions Chennai Super Kings in a contest dripping with pedigree and pressure. When red meets yellow in Bengaluru, the stakes rarely need selling, and this one arrives with momentum on one side and urgency on the other.

RCB enter this encounter high on confidence after a commanding start to their campaign. That opening win showcased depth and dominance, with the batting unit clicking in unison. Devdutt Padikkal, Virat Kohli and Rajat Patidar all found runs with authority, setting the tone early. A brief gap since that win has only sharpened the anticipation, and RCB will be keen to pick up exactly where they left off, especially on a surface that rewards fearless strokeplay.

Chennai Super Kings, however, walk in desperate for lift off. Two games in and yet to register a win, CSK find themselves searching for rhythm amid growing injury concerns. The absence of MS Dhoni for nearly a month and Dewald Brevis still on the recovery trail has stretched their resources. Still, there were positive signs in the last outing as Mhatre delivered a fluent 73 at a healthy strike rate, well backed by Shivam Dube’s late flourish. Those sparks will need to turn into a sustained flame.

History, hunger and home advantage collide under Bengaluru lights. One side looks to cement authority, the other to rescue momentum. As noise swells and nerves tighten, the question looms large. Can CSK script a comeback or will the Defending champions continue their charge?
Matchsummary.PostMatchCommentary:
Tim David (Player of the match):
“Obviously very pleased - it doesn’t always pan out this way. Rajat was absolutely flying at one end while I played my role, and to get us to a strong total and put pressure on the opposition was really satisfying.
I feel lucky to bat in different positions without changing my game much. All the preparation gives me confidence, along with the backing from teammates and support staff. Batting with hitters like Jitesh and Sheppy behind you makes it even easier.
Working with DK has been invaluable - his experience in these conditions really shows. You keep your basics, keep improving, and try not to put too much pressure on yourself. When you play high-risk cricket, you accept the ups and downs.
As for the 106 metre six - we joke about hitting the roof in training, so to get one sweet out of the middle in a match feels pretty special!”

Rajat Patidar (Royal Challengers Bengaluru Captain):
“Of course, it feels great to be there. But at the same time, when you play good cricket, the real satisfaction comes from that performance rather than just the position on the table.”
“Early on, the ball was holding up a little. The way Phil and Virat bhai handled that phase was outstanding. After that, Dev and Tim David took charge - I thoroughly enjoyed watching all those sixes, both from the dugout and from the non-striker’s end.”



Ruturaj Gaikwad (Chennai Super Kings Captain):
"I was a bit surprised we crossed two hundred in the end and credit to Sarfaraz, Overton, Veer and Dube for the fight they showed. If I had contributed more myself the result might have been different and I take responsibility for the loss today. With David it was an unlucky moment because we almost had his wicket but it turned out to be an illegal delivery and after that he played a top class innings. We could have had the powerplay momentum if we had taken the early chance of Kohli. We were still in the game till around the thirteenth or fourteenth over but let the momentum slip after that."



Royal Challengers Bengaluru produced a batting display of rare ferocity at the Chinnaswamy Stadium, overwhelming Chennai Super Kings with a commanding 43 run victory in a match where records and milestones blended with sustained dominance.

Put in to bat, Bengaluru surged to a colossal 250 for 3, scoring at 12.5 an over across the innings. Phil Salt provided early thrust with 46 off 30 balls, while Devdutt Padikkal struck a fluent 50 from 29 to keep the tempo high through the middle overs. The decisive phase arrived at the death, where Rajat Patidar and Tim David unleashed relentless power. The pair added an unbeaten 99 runs in just 35 balls, Patidar finishing on 48 from 19, while David dominated the evening with a breathtaking 70 not out off 25, clearing the ropes eight times as Bengaluru collected 99 runs between overs 15 and 20.

Chennai’s response showed fight but never control. After collapsing to 30 for 3 inside three overs, Sarfaraz Khan countered with a rapid 50 from 25 balls, while Prashant Veer’s 43 and Jamie Overton’s 37 pushed the total past 200. The chase ended at 207 in 19.4 overs.

Bhuvneshwar Kumar played a crucial role with the ball, finishing with 3 for 41 and reaching the landmark of 200 IPL wickets, a testament to his longevity and skill. His milestone performance underlined a night firmly coloured in Bengaluru red.

The first game of Sunday’s double-header shifts focus to the Orange Army as Sunrisers Hyderabad return to familiar surroundings for their first home fixture of the season at Uppal. They take on the Lucknow Super Giants in what promises to be an intriguing contest.

Sunrisers Hyderabad head into this clash with renewed confidence after a spirited win in Kolkata. In doing so, they became the first side this season to successfully defend a total, bouncing back strongly from their opening defeat. With a formidable top order featuring Abhishek Sharma, Travis Head, and skipper Ishan Kishan, the hosts will be eager to build momentum and kickstart a winning streak in front of their home crowd.

Lucknow Super Giants, on the other hand, have questions to address following a disappointing start with the bat in their opening loss, where they were restricted to 141. For Lucknow to challenge effectively, their overseas core of Marsh, Aiden Markram, and Nicholas Pooran will need to step up. Their pace attack, however, showed promise in the previous outing and could play a crucial role once again.

With both teams looking to assert themselves early in the tournament, this contest sets up as a compelling start to Sunday’s action.

Lucknow Super Giants completed a composed chase at Hyderabad to defeat Sunrisers Hyderabad by five wickets, after controlling the game through discipline with the ball and a calm finish with the bat.

Sunrisers were put under pressure early after opting to bat. Mohammed Shami produced a superb opening spell, finishing with 2 for 9 from four overs and reducing the hosts to 8 for 2 inside three overs. At 26 for 4 in the eighth over, Hyderabad were struggling before Heinrich Klaasen and Nitish Kumar Reddy mounted a strong recovery. Klaasen struck a fluent 62 from 41 balls, while Nitish added power and intent with 56 from 33, the pair adding 116 runs for the fifth wicket and lifting the total to a competitive 156 for 9. Prince Yadav and Avesh Khan supported Shami well, combining for four wickets and keeping the run rate in check.

Lucknow’s chase was built on stability rather than speed. Aiden Markram gave early impetus with 45 from 27 balls, taking the score to 77 by the ninth over. Rishabh Pant then anchored the innings with an unbeaten 68 from 50 deliveries, striking nine boundaries and absorbing pressure through the middle. Despite brief stutters that left Lucknow at 139 for 5 in the eighteenth over, Pant held firm to guide the side to 160 for 5 in 19.5 overs..

In 41 matches, he’s piled up an impressive 1,806 runs. He is the very definition of silky consistency and scoreboard pressure. Those numbers scream reliability with intent — the kind of batter who anchors an innings yet shifts gears seamlessly when the moment demands.

MATCH PREVIEW

Match number nine of the TATA IPL 2026 brings the spotlight to Ahmedabad as the Narendra Modi Stadium lights up for the first time this season, with Gujarat Titans squaring off against Rajasthan Royals in a clash rich with recent history. These were the finalists of the 2022 edition, and while circumstances are different now, the edge and expectation remain firmly intact.

Gujarat Titans walk into this contest under pressure, still searching for their first points of the season. Their previous outing against Punjab Kings exposed a fragile middle order, as GT failed to capitalise on promising starts from the top three and were restricted to a sub 170 total in a tight defeat. One shining positive, however, was Prasidh Krishna, whose fiery three wicket burst nearly turned the game on its head. GT will be desperate for a more complete performance tonight as they look to get their campaign up and running.

Rajasthan Royals, in contrast, arrive with confidence flowing. They opened their season with an emphatic eight wicket victory, dismantling Chennai Super Kings with ruthless efficiency. Their bowlers set the tone early, applying relentless pressure, before the chase was lit up by Sooryavanshi, who produced a breathtaking 15 ball fifty, the fastest of IPL 2026 so far. It was a statement win that underlined both intent and depth.

Momentum favours the Royals, urgency fuels the Titans. Ahmedabad promises pace, bounce and big moments, with both sides knowing how quickly seasons can swing. As memories of 2022 resurface and the stakes rise under the lights, the question echoes through the stands. Who takes control tonight, desperation or dominance?
Matchsummary.PostMatchCommentary:
Ravi Bishnoi (Player of the Match):
"It was a tough season last year and I realised whenever I missed my length I was getting punished, so I focused on tightening that area and accepting the result if batters still hit me. It took mental, technical and physical effort together and I bowled a lot of deliveries to keep improving. My favourite wicket was Rahul Tewatia because he is known to change games in such situations and his dismissal was crucial. If he had stayed, the match could have gone either way. The death bowling from Tushar and Jofra showed how collective the effort was, and as a young team we want to keep entertaining."
 

Riyan Parag (Rajasthan Royals Captain):
"The last two overs were simply incredible and taking the call to bowl full and fast paid off because the boys executed exactly what was planned. I was extremely excited watching them deliver under pressure. I was close to changing the order but Jurel backed Jofra for the nineteenth and that turned out to be a great call. The idea was to bowl as quick and straight as possible at the end and the execution was brilliant. Jurel has done the hard work batting lower down and now at three he has the chance to score big and hopefully lead us to the title."


Rashid Khan (Gujarat Titans Captain):

"We bowled really well overall, especially after the strong start they made, and with the bat too we began nicely before losing back-to-back wickets, which pushed us on the back foot. That phase cost us momentum and on a surface like this scoring nine or ten an over is manageable if you keep the boundaries coming. Losing quick wickets in the middle did not allow us to finish the innings the way we wanted. Everyone has their own game plan but reading conditions and match requirements is crucial and it is still early in the tournament so we will learn and come back stronger. In the final over the talk was about finding one boundary, Tushar executed his yorkers well and I should have taken the chance when he missed, we stay calm, learn from this and hopefully Shubman will be fine for the next game."


Rajasthan Royals held their nerve in a high-scoring encounter at Ahmedabad, completing a tight six-run victory over Gujarat Titans after both sides traded punches through all forty overs in a contest defined by sustained scoring and late tension.

Batting first, Rajasthan posted an imposing 210 for 6, built around a fluent 75 from Dhruv Jurel off 42 balls at a strike rate nearing 180. Yashasvi Jaiswal set the base with 55 from 36 deliveries, putting on 126 for the first two wickets as Rajasthan reached the halfway mark at 113 for 1. Support arrived in bursts, with Shimron Hetmyer striking 18 off 8 and the Royals scoring at over ten an over in 14 of the 20 overs. Gujarat’s bowlers struggled for control, conceding 13 wides, with Rabada finishing with 2 for 42.

Gujarat’s reply stayed competitive throughout. Sai Sudharsan anchored the chase superbly with 73 from 44 balls, bringing up his fifty in just 33 deliveries as Gujarat crossed 100 by the tenth over. A sharp collapse followed as Ravi Bishnoi ripped through the middle order with figures of 4 for 41, removing four batters between overs 12 and 15 to swing momentum Rajasthan’s way. Rashid Khan and Kagiso Rabada mounted a late surge, adding 47 in the final five overs, but the ask proved just beyond reach.

Gujarat closed on 204 for 8, falling short despite scoring at over ten an over in 11 overs, as Rajasthan’s middle overs control proved decisive in a thriller decided by fine margins.

Eden Gardens in Kolkata has traditionally favored high-scoring matches, with teams batting first winning seven times and sides chasing prevailing in six encounters. The average first-innings score at the venue is 199, with teams posting around 58 runs in the powerplay and facing a stiff challenge in the death overs, where the run rate climbs to 12.2. The highest successful chase recorded here is 262/2, highlighting the batting-friendly nature of the pitch, especially under lights when dew plays a role. Pace bowlers have been more successful overall, accounting for 68% of wickets, while spinners have claimed the remaining 32%, mainly exploiting the middle overs. Teams batting first aim to set a big total, but chasing sides have an almost equal chance of victory, making strategic planning for toss and bowling rotations crucial at this historically iconic stadium.
 

Kolkata Knight Riders host Sunrisers Hyderabad at Eden Gardens on Thursday, 2 April, in what promises to be a high-scoring encounter. Both teams are looking to recover after their opening games, where they posted 200+ totals but failed to defend, exposing vulnerabilities in their bowling attacks.

Their batting lineup, anchored by Klaasen and Travis Head, will need to fire to counter KKR’s spin threat. Eden Gardens’ dew factor may assist the chasing side, making the toss crucial.

With home advantage, a settled spin duo, and in-form top-order batsmen, KKR are slight favorites, while SRH must rely on big individual performances to turn the tide.
